end.summary:
Practised multiplying numbers ending in zeros by multiplying non-zero parts and counting zeros.
Rudra correctly solved 60 × 700 = 42,000, 6,000 × 50 = 300,000, and 50 × 1,000 = 50,000.
Rudra gave 6,000 × 500 as 300,000; the extra zero was not yet included when last seen.
Practised estimating large products by rounding first; teach-back was not yet passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised breaking numbers into non-zero parts and counting the zeros, along with rounding before estimating products. Rudra used the method correctly for several examples, including 60 × 700 and 6,000 × 50. One mix-up remained with 6,000 × 500, where a zero was dropped; it was not corrected later in the lesson. At home, practise two examples each day by writing the non-zero multiplication first and then counting every zero together.
